newsitem.title: USA: Tender offer initiated for Ill. incinerator bonds.
newsitem.headline: Tender offer initiated for Ill. incinerator bonds.

text.p: A Chicago suburb has initiated a tender offer for nearly $320 million of bonds sold for a waste incinerator, Foster Wheeler Corp. announced Wednesday.

According to the announcement, owners of the resource recovery revenue bonds sold by Robbins, Ill., in 1994 will be able to exchange their series A and B bonds for restructured bonds under the tender.
The tender offer began Wednesday and will last until Oct. 7, the firm said. The exchange will be completed on Oct. 15 if 96 percent of the bonds are tendered.

The announcement followed action last month by Foster Wheeler's board of directors to approve the bond restructuring in the wake of the enactment of an Illinois law that repealed a state subsidy for the Robbins incinerator.
The incinerator was developed by Illinois subsidiaries of the Clinton, N.J.-based firm.

Under the restructuring announced in May, the bonds will have additional credit support, the benefit of additional covenants, different redemption provisions, a lower interest rate and, in some cases, extended maturity dates. Exchange offer materials are being circulated through Georgeson & Co. Inc., New York, N.Y., as Information Agent.
A lawsuit filed by Foster Wheeler against state of Illinois officials challenging the lost incinerator subsidy is pending in U.S. District Court in Chicago.

The lawsuit claims Illinois' repeal earlier this year of a guarentee allowing incinerators to sell their electricity to utilities at a higher rate subsidized by the state violated the contract clause of the constitution.
